newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER SHOWCASE-RONALDO GOAL SETTLES ANGRY DERBY.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER SHOWCASE-RONALDO GOAL SETTLES ANGRY DERBY.

text.p: A solitary goal from Brazilian striker Ronaldo gave Barcelona a 1-0 win over Real Madrid in a bad-tempered league clash between Spain's arch-rivals on Saturday.
Both teams were lucky to end the game with 11 players after a disappointing match which leaves Real a commanding five points clear of Barcelona with as many games remaining.

After losing to Real 2-0 earlier in the season, Barcelona will have to take six more points than Real to lift the title, as results of games between teams level on points are used to decide final positions before goal difference.
Real coach Fabio Capello played down the importance of the result.

"Nothing's happened. We have five points' advantage, well six points," said Capello "The result was not fair, in the second half there was only one team on the pitch... Their fans helped their side a lot."

Supporters in the Camp Nou stadium had to wait until the 40th minute to see the first clear shot on goal. But a rash of chances for both sides just before halftime ended with Roberto Carlos bringing down Barcelona winger Luis Figo in the area.
Ronaldo saw his penalty saved by Bodo Illgner, but Figo kept his head to clip the ball back, and the Brazilian knocked in his 32nd goal of the season.
With Real's constant pressing tactics stifling the Barcelona attack, Ronaldo had a quiet game.
Barcelona's offensive strategy had been stunted after just 15 minutes when Roberto Carlos brought down Giovanni, the man brought in to add bite to the home side's attack.
The Barcelona playmaker had to be carried off, and shortly afterwards Miguel Angel Nadal went the same way after another badly-timed challenge from Roberto Carlos.
Real's Brazilian full-back seemed to be unnerved by an angry reaction from Barcelona fans, whom he had accused of racism earlier in the season.
Some fans displayed a banner with a racist jibe apparently directed at Roberto Carlos.
Lax refereeing early in the match from an inexperienced official added to the problems on the pitch.
At one stage he failed to spot Barcelona's fiery Bulgarian forward Hristo Stoichkov spitting at Real defender Christian Panucci.
Barcelona coach Bobby Robson was in no doubt as to how the referee should have controlled the players.

"Roberto Carlos is a fantastic player, but today I think he was very lucky, and he could have been expelled twice. And I'm not referring to the tackles on Giovanni and Nadal. The penalty was also a yellow card."
But Robson also had praise for his own side.
"We had to change the team three times... I'm proud of the players, they showed great attitude...We are five or six points back, it was important to win," he said.

Robson's men had nearly seen their outside chance of taking the first division championship disappear when Predrag Mijatovic lobbed over after a goalmouth mix-up had left him unmarked 10 minutes from time.

Mijatovic and strike partner Davor Suker had also wasted opportunities at the beginning of the second half. But Real failed to find a shot on goal at all apart from that, and on balance Barcelona deserved the result.
The bad tempers on the field were echoed in the president's box, where Capello clashed with several members of the Barcelona board.
